mcqs.question: A convex lens has a focal length of +20 cm. An object is placed very far away (practically at infinity). Using the lens formula, what is the correct image distance?
mcqs.explanation: For an object at infinity, 1/u ≈ 0. The lens formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u reduces to 1/v = 1/f, so v = f = +20 cm. The image is real and formed on the opposite side of the lens, giving a positive image distance. Options B, C and D arise from common sign or magnitude mistakes.

mcqs.question: A concave (diverging) lens has a focal length of -12 cm. An object is placed 15 cm in front of the lens. According to the Cartesian sign convention, what is the sign of the image distance v?
mcqs.explanation: A concave lens always forms a virtual image on the same side as the object. In the Cartesian sign convention, distances measured opposite to the direction of incident light (the side of the object) are taken as negative. Hence the image distance v is negative. Positive would correspond to a real image on the opposite side, which never occurs for a diverging lens. Zero would mean the image at the lens, and "cannot be determined" is incorrect because the sign is fixed by lens type.

mcqs.question: Lens A is a convex lens with focal length +10 cm and an object placed 30 cm in front of it. Lens B is a concave lens with focal length -15 cm and an object also placed 30 cm in front of it. Which lens produces a larger magnitude of magnification?

options.C: Both lenses give the same magnitude

mcqs.explanation: For Lens A (convex): 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/10 - (-1/30) = 0.1333, so v = 7.5 cm. Magnification m = v/u = 7.5/(-30) = -0.25 (|m| = 0.25). For Lens B (concave): 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = -1/15 - (-1/30) = -0.0333, so v = -30 cm. Magnification m = v/u = (-30)/(-30) = +1 (|m| = 1). Hence Lens B gives a larger magnitude of magnification. Options A and C are therefore incorrect, and D is wrong because both lenses do form images (real for A, virtual for B).

mcqs.question: The optical power P of a thin lens is defined as:

options.A: The reciprocal of its focal length measured in centimeters
options.B: The product of its focal length and the refractive index of the material
options.C: The reciprocal of its focal length measured in meters
options.D: The focal length divided by the speed of light

mcqs.answer: The reciprocal of its focal length measured in meters
mcqs.explanation: Power P (in dioptres) = 1/f, where f is the focal length in meters. This definition allows direct addition of powers for thin lenses placed in contact. Option A uses centimeters, giving a value 100 times larger than the correct dioptre value. Option B mixes unrelated quantities, and option D is unrelated to optics. Hence C is correct.
